source.citation: Shafiro, Boris, Kachanov, Mark (1997). Materials with fluid-filled pores of various shapes: Effective elastic properties and fluid pressure polarization. International Journal of Solids and Structures 34(27), 3517-3540.
source.location: Eqs (6)-(14) (pp. 3521-3523), captions of Figs 4 and 5 and the text between them (pp. 3524-3525)

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), on page images rendered at 120 dpi; equations, captions and labels read on the images, the extracted text being garbled
transcription.note: The fluid is given by its compressibility kappa (MPa^-1), the matrix by E0 (MPa) and nu0. The pressure q in a cavity is q = Q : sigma, eq. (6), positive in compression, sigma being the remote stress (tension positive). The compressibility of the dry cavity is C_p = R/E0, that of the matrix C0 = 3(1 - 2 nu0)/E0, and delta = (kappa - C0)/C_p, eq. (8). The aspect ratio is zeta = a3/a, a3 the semi-axis along the axis of symmetry n of the spheroid. Fig. 4 plots q/T against the angle phi between n and the direction of a uniaxial compression T; Fig. 5 plots q/P against zeta under a hydrostatic pressure P.

E0.location: Captions of Figs 4, 6, 7 and 8; label of Fig. 5
E0.description: Young modulus of the granite matrix (6 x 10^4 MPa).

nu0.location: Captions of Figs 4, 6, 7 and 8; label of Fig. 5
nu0.description: Poisson ratio of the granite matrix.

kappa_water.location: Captions of Figs 4, 6, 7 and 8; label of Fig. 5
kappa_water.description: Compressibility of the water filling the pores (0.5 x 10^-3 MPa^-1), the inverse of its bulk modulus.

amplification_sphere.description: Largest ratio q/P under hydrostatic pressure, reached by a sphere for an incompressible fluid (kappa = 0) and nu0 = 0.

amplification_needle.location: Text p. 3524 ("almost as high (~2.5) in the limit of a needle")
amplification_needle.description: Ratio q/P of a needle for kappa = 0 and nu0 = 0.

amplification_crack_slope.description: Slope of q/P against the aspect ratio of a narrow crack-like spheroid, kappa = 0 and nu0 = 0.

closed_forms.Q: -n n/(1 + delta), delta = zeta pi (kappa E0 - 3(1 - 2 nu0))/(4(1 - nu0^2))
q = P/(1 + delta) = C_p P/(C_p + kappa - C0)

notes: The curve of Fig. 5 for kappa = 0 and nu0 = 0.5 (incompressible matrix) is q/P = 1 at every aspect ratio, as eq. (14) gives with C0 = 0.
